## Introduction

Data Wrangling with dplyr and tidyr

### Package installation

```{r}
if (!require(dplyr)) install.packages("dplyr")
if (!require(tidyr)) install.packages("tidyr")
if (!require(data.table)) install.packages("data.table")
if (!require(DataExplorer)) install.packages("DataExplorer")
if (!require(ggplot2)) install.packages("ggplot2")

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(data.table)
library(DataExplorer)
```

## Task 2: Data Wrangling and Visualization

```{r}
glimpse(myLCdata_dirty)
str(myLCdata_dirty)

summary(myLCdata_dirty)
```

| Variable       | Explanation |
|----------------|-------------|
| annual_inc     | numerical   |
| open_acc       | numerical   |
| purpose        | categorical |
| home_ownership | categorical |
| inq_last_6mths | numerical   |

: Explanation of the variables (categorical or numeric)

Empty categorical features can contain the following values:

-   **`NA` or Not Available:** Indicates missing values that R recognizes as missing.
-   **The string `"n/a"`:** We pretend this string was used in the source data set to indicate missing data. Since it is a string R does not recognize it as missing.
-   **A space `" "`:** Another special string.
-   **The empty string `""`:** Another special string.

Empty numerical features can contain the following values:

-   **`NA`:** Standard missing values.
-   **`NaN` or Not a Number:** Results from invalid computations such as 0/0.
-   **Outliers:** These were actually not ingested but already present in the data. There is no rigid mathematical definition of what constitutes an outlier. In this task we use Tukey's fences. We count values as outliers if they lie outside the whiskers of the boxplot.

### Overall NA per feature

```{r}
myLCdata_dirty %>% summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.))))
```

#### Categorical features (purpose, home_ownership)

```{r}
myLCdata_dirty_values_categorical <- myLCdata_dirty %>%
  select(purpose, home_ownership) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "columns", values_to = "empty_value") %>%
  filter(if_any(everything(), ~ . %in% c(" ", "", "n/a") | is.na(.))) %>%
  mutate(empty_value = case_when(
    empty_value == "" ~ "empty_string",
    empty_value == " " ~ "single_space",
    is.na(empty_value) ~ "NA_value",
    empty_value == "n/a" ~ "n/a"
  )) %>%
  group_by(columns, empty_value) %>% summarise(dirty_value_count = n()) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = empty_value, values_from=dirty_value_count, names_prefix = "percentage_") %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~. / nrow(myLCdata_dirty)))

head(myLCdata_dirty_values_categorical)

ggplot_data_categorical <- myLCdata_dirty_values_categorical %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols=-columns, names_to = "empty_value", values_to = "proportion")

ggplot(ggplot_data_categorical) +
  geom_col(aes(x = columns, y = proportion)) +
  coord_flip() + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  facet_wrap(~empty_value, ncol = 1)
```

#### Numerical features (annual_inc, open_acc,inq_last_6mths)

```{r}
myLCdata_dirty %>%
  summarise(na_count = sum(is.na(annual_inc)) - sum(is.nan(annual_inc)))
myLCdata_dirty %>% 
  summarise(NAN_values = sum(is.nan(annual_inc)))

boxplot.stats(myLCdata_dirty$annual_inc)

ggplot(myLCdata_dirty) + geom_boxplot(aes(y=annual_inc)) + scale_y_log10()
```

```{r}

# all rows
nrow(myLCdata_dirty)

# is.na() returns TRUE for both NA and NaN, however is. nan() return TRUE for NaN (0/0) and FALSE for NA
myLCdata_dirty %>% select(annual_inc, open_acc, inq_last_6mths) %>% filter(if_any(everything(), ~is.na(.))) %>% summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.))))
```

```{r}
# just NA values
myLCdata_dirty %>% 
  select(annual_inc, open_acc, inq_last_6mths) %>% 
  filter(if_any(everything(), ~is.na(.))) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.))-sum(is.nan(.))))

# just NAN values
myLCdata_dirty %>% 
  select(annual_inc, open_acc, inq_last_6mths) %>% 
  filter(if_any(everything(), ~is.na(.))) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.nan(.))))

# outliers in features
myLCdata_dirty %>% 
  select(annual_inc, open_acc, inq_last_6mths) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~length(boxplot.stats(.x)$out)))
```

```{r}
# proportional table of NA and NAN values
table_NA_NAN_perc <- myLCdata_dirty %>% 
  select(annual_inc, open_acc, inq_last_6mths) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "feature", values_to = "values") %>%
  filter(if_any(everything(), ~is.na(.))) %>%
  group_by(feature, values) %>%
  summarise(count = n()) %>%
  mutate(across(is.numeric, ~./nrow(myLCdata_dirty))) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = values, values_from = count, names_prefix = "percentage_")
```

```{r}
# length of outliers
table_outliers_perc <- myLCdata_dirty %>% 
  select(annual_inc, open_acc, inq_last_6mths) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~length(boxplot.stats(.x)$out))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "feature", values_to = "percentage_outliers") %>%
  mutate(across(is.numeric, ~./nrow(myLCdata_dirty)))
```

```{r}
#Joining the two tables together (I understand it could be done quicker, but I wanted to test all the functionalities of dplyr)
analysis_missing_numeric <- table_NA_NAN_perc %>% inner_join(table_outliers_perc, by="feature")
analysis_missing_numeric
```

```{r}
#The same just shorter (from Gemini for reference)
myLCdata_dirty %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      c(annual_inc, open_acc, inq_last_6mths),
      list(
        percentage_NaN = ~ sum(is.nan(.x)) / n(),
        percentage_NA = ~ sum(is.na(.x) & !is.nan(.x)) / n(),
        percentage_outliers = ~ length(boxplot.stats(.x)$out) / n()
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("feature", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(percentage_.*)"
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot_data_numeric <- analysis_missing_numeric %>%
  pivot_longer(-feature, names_to = "type", values_to = "values")

ggplot(ggplot_data_numeric) + 
  geom_col(aes(x=feature, y=values)) + 
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  facet_wrap(~type, ncol = 1)
```
